summary: Iberian Gauge is a lighter entry in Amabel Holland's 'Gauge' series of stock-and-track train games, where players buy shares in railroad companies and then use those shares to build track across Iberia's rugged hex map. It's a tighter, faster take on 18xx-style stock manipulation without the full complexity of a traditional 18xx title.
praised: accessible entry point into stock-holding train game mechanics
criticised: can feel swingy if stock prices crash early
less depth than full 18xx games for veteran train gamers
leasing/track rules take a round to fully grasp
map interaction can feel limited with fewer players

interaction.kind: route-building and blocking on a shared map
interaction.detail: Every company's track goes onto the same hex map, so a spur one company builds can block the cheapest path for a rival company, and leasing rules force players to negotiate track access economically rather than diplomatically. Ownership is via stock, so most of the game state (the map, share prices) is shared, while a player's own holdings are private.

sources: Stock/company value (net worth from shares held)
scoring.how_you_win: Victory points double as money: you earn them through company income and spend them to build or lease track, so you win by balancing expansion against hoarding VP, ending with the highest total when the game triggers its end.
scoring.score_note: cash+share value; scales with player count
